dog.description_text:
Meet Homeland! 🐾

Affectionately known as Maggie in her foster home!

Short Bio:

Meet Homeland, a sweet, playful, and curious little girl with a big love for other dogs and an adventurous spirit! Her foster family calls her Maggie, and she’s already stealing their hearts.

Homeland may be a little shy when first meeting humans, but give her some time and you’ll see her adorable personality start to shine. She absolutely LOVES other dogs! Meeting her foster family’s resident dogs was a turning point for her, and she quickly came out of her shell, running around, playing, and making new friends.

She’s a curious little explorer and a quick learner who picks up on new things surprisingly fast. She’s currently mastering stairs, building confidence on the leash, and learning that human affection can be a wonderful thing.

Homeland is still very much a puppy, with plenty of playful energy, but she also has a gentle, respectful side. She’s a little more outgoing and adventurous than her sister and loves discovering new things.

While she’s still learning to trust human touch, she’s making wonderful progress every day. With patience, love, and a little encouragement from a furry friend, Homeland is sure to continue blossoming into the amazing dog she’s meant to be!

Personality & Characteristics:

My foster dog is good with:

- Dogs: YES! Absolutely loves other dogs and wants to be everyone’s friend.
- Kids: Yes! Currently living with children ages 6 and 9. She’s comfortable around them but doesn’t actively seek out their attention just yet.
- Cats: Not yet tested.

My foster dog is:

- Crate trained: Does great sleeping overnight in a pen with her sister.
- House trained: Work in progress! She’s doing well with frequent outdoor breaks and can hold it overnight, but she’s still learning.
- Low shed: Yes!

3 Keywords for your pup: Playful, Gentle, Curious

Energy Level (1 = calm, 10 = high energy): 7/10

Barker? Or Quiet Pup?: Very quiet so far! She hasn’t shown much interest in barking, although she may find her voice as she becomes more comfortable.

Walking Manners: Still building confidence on the leash. She’ll benefit from patient encouragement and continued practice.

Appetite: Good! She’s a funny little eater who likes to take a bit of food from her bowl, carry it back to her bed, and enjoy it there.

Favorite Things: Playing with her sister, making friends with other dogs, running around, and exploring her surroundings.

Commands/Tricks: Still learning! Homeland is a quick learner and is currently working on building confidence and mastering new experiences.

Additional Notes: Homeland would love a home with patient humans who understand that she’s still learning to trust and enjoy human affection. A friendly, playful resident dog could be a wonderful companion and confidence booster for her. She’s a sweet little girl with so much potential, and watching her blossom has been such a joy

: ALL adoptions require a completed application and final contract. The application can be found at WaldosRescue.org and once you are approved to adopt you will be put in touch with the foster to see if it's a good match. We are a RESCUE not a shelter. We conduct veterinary and personal reference checks during the application approval process. We are unable to contact every applicant for every dog. We will select the best applicant for each dog, based on the dogs needs. Waldos Rescue Pen is a 501c3 whose primary focus is rescuing dogs from the euthanasia list from high kill shelters throughout the United States and Korea.
